claim: In the large-population household branching model with path-shaped households and independent within-household edge transmission probability \(p=1/2\), the laws \(q^A_1=q^A_3=1/2\) and \(q^B_1=1/3,q^B_2=1/2,q^B_4=1/6\) have the same household-size mean \(2\) and variance \(1\), but for every external-infection mean \(\beta\in(8/13,48/77)\) they straddle the invasion threshold: \(\mathcal R_*^A=13\beta/8>1\) and \(\mathcal R_*^B=77\beta/48<1\). In particular, at \(\beta=31/50\), the exact values are \(403/400\) and \(2387/2400\).

scientific_limitations_and_integrity.integrity: Rational calculations are reproduced in RESULT.md; cited household-model assumptions are stated explicitly.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.not_proved: No claim for arbitrary within-household contact graphs, arbitrary transmission laws, empirical populations, finite-population final size, or universal novelty.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.proved: Exact formulas \(\mathcal R_*^A=13\beta/8\) and \(\mathcal R_*^B=77\beta/48\), exact moment matching, and opposite sides of the branching invasion threshold throughout the stated nonempty \(\beta\) interval.

title: Moment-identical household sizes can straddle the invasion threshold under path transmission
